atoms.b: This ((++bar_chart line_chart)) shows the CO<sub>2</sub> emissions of planes and train rides in Germany per person.
It compares the ((++emissions size)) of both means of transport per route.
((++Three Six)) different routes are displayed: Berlin to Cologne, Munich to Hamburg, and Cologne to Munich.
The numbers represent ((++the_outward_and_return a_single)) journey by the means of transport.
All figures of plane emissions are ((++drastically_higher drastically_lower slightly_higher)) than those of trains.
On average, ((++plane_emissions train_emissions)) for domestic journeys are ten times higher than ((++train_emissions plane_emissions)).
On the distance from Berlin to Cologne and back, a plane emits ((++298 310 238)) kg CO<sub>2</sub> per person, while the train only emits ((++27.6 37.4 41)) kg CO<sub>2</sub>.

Plane emissions are ((++lower the_same higher)) for the distance from Cologne to Munich and back than Berlin to Cologne and back. On average a plane emits 238 kg CO<sub>2</sub> per person on these flights.
The train, on the other hand, produces more emissions on the route from Cologne to Munich and back than ((++on_the_other_journeys the_plane)): 41 kg CO<sub>2</sub> per person.
The ((++highest lowest slightest)) figure on the chart shows the emission of a plane going from Munich to Hamburg and back. It causes 310 kg of CO<sub>2</sub> emissions per person.

instruction.text: Was kann man aus diesem Diagramm schließen? Mehrere Antworten sind richtig.

hint.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>amount</voice> bedeutet Menge <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m2'>pollution</voice> bedeutet Verschmutzung

b: ++Planes produce massive amounts of CO<sub>2</sub> emissions compared to trains.
Trains aren't a good alternative to planes because trains produce as much CO<sub>2</sub> as planes.
++For domestic journeys train travel can be preferable because it causes less pollution for the environment than planes.
